---
title: "Documentation"
---

`repo-familiar` uses the [Divio documentation system](https://docs.divio.com/documentation-system/) as the default structure for project documentation.

The goal is to keep each page useful for both humans and agents by making its job explicit before writing it.

## Four Documentation Types

- **Tutorials** are learning-oriented lessons. They take a newcomer through concrete steps with visible results.
- **How-to guides** are goal-oriented recipes. They solve a specific task for someone who already has enough context to ask the question.
- **Reference** is information-oriented description. It records commands, flags, APIs, schemas, configuration, generated assets, and other machinery.
- **Explanation** is understanding-oriented context. It covers architecture, tradeoffs, ADRs, domain concepts, and why decisions were made.

## Generated Quarto Sites

Generated downstream repositories include Quarto pages for all four types:

- `docs/tutorials.qmd`
- `docs/how-to.qmd`
- `docs/reference.qmd`
- `docs/explanation.qmd`

Existing pages can keep their familiar names, but their purpose should stay clear. For example, `docs/usage.qmd` usually belongs with how-to guides, while `docs/architecture.qmd` and `docs/adr/` usually belong with explanation.

## Agent Guidance

When an agent edits documentation, it should first classify the page by type. If a page starts mixing purposes, prefer linking across sections instead of collapsing the structure:

- A tutorial can link to reference details instead of listing every option.
- A how-to guide can link to explanation instead of pausing for background theory.
- Reference can link to how-to guides instead of becoming a task walkthrough.
- Explanation can link to tutorials or how-to guides instead of instructing step by step.
